Ingest organisation websites

Source: R/md-ingest-websites.R
md_ingest_websites.Rd

Builds the website table from every source that carries a website field: the 990 filing header (F9_00_ORG_WEBSITE), the 1023-EZ approvals (Orgurl) and the 990-N e-Postcard (website). One row per (ein, site_key, source). Rebuilt whole on each call, like the derived tables, because three sources feed it and n_eins_sharing spans all three.

Usage

md_ingest_websites(
  con = NULL,
  efile_version = NULL,
  f1023ez_version = NULL,
  e_postcard_version = NULL
)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

efile_version

Pinned efile_header version, or NULL to skip.

f1023ez_version

Pinned f1023ez version, or NULL to skip. Reads the CSVs md_ingest_f1023ez() converted, so run that first.

e_postcard_version

Pinned e_postcard version, or NULL to skip.

Value

Row counts per source, invisibly.

Details

A website is strong evidence when it is specific to one organisation and worthless when it is not, so the table records which is which rather than leaving it to every consumer.

What counts as a website

The fields are free text, and much of it is not a website: N/A, NONE, TBD, SEE SCHEDULE O, UNDER CONSTRUCTION, an organisation's name, even xxx-xx-xxxx. Rather than list placeholders, a value is kept only if, after cleaning, its host is a valid domain name: dot-separated labels of letters, digits and hyphens ending in a 2-24 letter top-level domain. Cleaning lowercases, turns a comma into a dot (www,ptk.org is a common typo), and strips the scheme, a leading www. and any port. A value with spaces in its host is not a website.

An email address (info@example.org) is kept by its domain, as kind = 'email', because an organisation's mail domain is usually its web domain. Mail from a personal provider (gmail.com, yahoo.com, ...) is dropped: it says nothing about which organisation sent it.

site_key

what a match would compare: For most sites site_key is the host without www.. For pages hosted on a shared platform (facebook.com, sites.google.com, a *.wixsite.com page, linktr.ee, ...) the host identifies the platform, not the organisation, so the key is the host plus the first path segment (facebook.com/hullscove), and is_platform is TRUE. A bare platform host with no path is dropped.

n_eins_sharing counts the EINs holding each site_key, across all sources. A national body's site written by thousands of chapters (elks.org) is family evidence, not identity evidence - the same distinction name_compact draws with its own n_eins_sharing.

Only known entities

A website needs an entity to belong to. Rows for EINs absent from entity are held back and counted, not admitted: the e-Postcard has 73,503 such EINs, and whether to admit them is a decision for an e-Postcard entity ingest, not for this one.
